correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives strict convexity of the scalar barrier objective and \(F_\delta′(0)=D(\mu)/\tau-\mu/\delta\), so zero targeting exists exactly when \(D(\mu)>0\) and then \(\delta_*=\tau\mu/D\). Substitution of \(\tau(\mu)=c\mu^a/(\mu^a+b)\) gives \(D(\mu)/\mu=x_2+\zeta c\mu^{a-1}/(\mu^a+b)\), from which the \(a>1\), \(a<1\), and strict \(a=1\) cases follow. On \(x_2+(c/b)\zeta=0\), exact cancellation gives \(D=x_2\mu^2/(\mu+b)>0\) and \(\delta_*=c/x_2\). The inspected verifier and independent arithmetic agree. The source paper prints a sign inconsistency in its displayed derivative, but its objective and denominator in equation (30) agree with the direct differentiation used here.

originality.rationale: The final claim is mechanically implied by two formulas printed in the same prior primary source. Equation (30) gives the zero-target relaxation with denominator \(\mu x_2+\tau\zeta\), including the requirement that the denominator be positive, and equation (32) gives exactly \(\tau(\mu)=c\mu^a/(\mu^a+b)\). Substituting equation (32) into equation (30) yields \(D(\mu)/\mu=x_2+\zeta c\mu^{a-1}/(\mu^a+b)\); the claimed exponent split and the critical coefficient identity are immediate elementary limits/algebra. Under implication-based originality, the fact that the source does not package that substitution as a named theorem does not make the corollary original.

final_claim: For the CCOpt scalar local endgame model with \(\tau(\mu)=c\mu^a/(\mu^a+b)\), the sign of \(D(\mu)=\mu x_2+\tau(\mu)\zeta\) yields a sharp transition at \(a=1\): zero targeting is eventually available for \(a>1\), unavailable for \(a<1\), and on \(a=1\) is controlled by \(L=x_2+(c/b)\zeta\), with the exact boundary \(L=0\) giving \(\delta_*(\mu)\equiv c/x_2\).
scientific_limitations: The mathematics is correct only for the scalar local model with fixed \(x_2\) and multiplier estimate as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
The final claim is rejected because it is a direct implication of equations (30) and (32) of the cited primary source, not because of an access or transport limitation.
